title: The Last Ledger
premise: In 1898, in the port city of Bellhaven, apprentice clockmaker Wendell Okonkwo is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and discovers hidden inside its case a second ledger — an unofficial census recording every person the official count erased: the deported, the drowned, the disappeared. When the census taker who kept it is found dead and the government's victors begin rewriting the city's history after a brutal quelling of the dockworkers' uprising, Wendell realizes he holds the only true record of who lived. Hunted by the historian charged with sanitizing the archives, Wendell and a found family of clockmakers, printers, and dockworkers race to verify the ledger, copy it, and get it on the public record before the official history is sealed. The book ends with Wendell testifying at the inquiry, the ledger read aloud into the record as the master clock strikes, and the original hidden once more — this time by choice, waiting for a future that will want the truth.
about_author: Xanthe Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging colonial census records and the silences between them. The Last Ledger is their second novel, written in a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. During the national census, Wendell gives the safe answers he has rehearsed for five years — until the census taker, Mr. Aldous Vane, asks about his sister, officially listed as deported but whom Wendell knows drowned in the harbor riots. Wendell's denial is too quick, and Vane's eyes sharpen. Beat: the fragile safety of silence cracking.

chapters.title: Twelve Bells, One Silence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Summoned to the observatory to repair the master clock, Wendell finds the mechanism sabotaged — deliberately, and recently. Inside the case, wedged among the gears, is a slim ledger in a hand he half-recognizes: names, dates, and causes of death for people the official record calls 'relocated.' Beat: dread mixed with a terrible sense of recognition.

chapters.title: The Hand in the Gears
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell identifies the handwriting as Vane's and returns to the census office to find it sealed, Vane reported drowned — an echo of his sister's fate. His mentor, Master Igeoma, warns him to return the ledger and forget it. Beat: the first offer of safe retreat, refused.

chapters.title: What the Printer Kept
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Sefu Ademola, a radical printer and dockworkers' widow's son, reveals Vane was his informant: the ledger is a counter-census Vane built from parish records, shipping manifests, and testimony. Sefu has half a duplicate already. Beat: Wendell stops being alone — the found family begins to assemble.

chapters.title: The Historian's Commission
chapters.summary: Cordelia Marsh's POV. The government appoints historian Cordelia Marsh to produce the official account of the riots before the anniversary. Brilliant and ambitious, she is told which conclusions to reach. She begins purging the archives — and requests the observatory clock's maintenance logs. Beat: the antagonist's competence makes her more frightening than cruelty would.

chapters.title: Names in the Margins
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell and Sefu cross-check ledger entries against parish books by candlelight. Wendell finds his sister's name — recorded as drowned, not deported — and grieves properly for the first time. Beat: the ledger becomes personal; the mission becomes a debt to the dead.

chapters.title: The Clockmaker's Oath
chapters.summary: Igeoma's POV. Master Igeoma recalls the night she hid a fugitive in the clock tower years ago and how Vane helped her, then went quiet. She realizes the ledger is her debt too, and instead of confiscating it, she teaches Wendell the tower's hiding places and escape routes. Beat: mentor becomes co-conspirator; found family deepens.

chapters.title: A Summons in Fine Print
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Cordelia summons Wendell to 'verify' the clock repair — a trap dressed as courtesy. Their interview is a fencing match: she quotes the official death toll, he corrects her with a detail only the ledger contains, and knows instantly he has said too much. Beat: the hunter now has a scent.

chapters.title: The Raid on Ademola Press
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Soldiers raze Sefu's print shop and seize his partial duplicate; Sefu escapes through the cellar with burns on his hands. Wendell hides him in the clock tower. Beat: the cost of the work becomes real, and the group shrinks to the committed.

chapters.title: What Vane Drowned For
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following Vane's coded marginal notes, Wendell retrieves Vane's source documents from a harbor customs locker — including a naval order authorizing the deportation ships to scuttle 'excess' passengers. Beat: horror hardens into purpose; the truth has a paper trail.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Approaches
chapters.summary: Cordelia's POV. Cordelia drafts the official history and feels the seams of her own omissions pulling. A clerk's slip shows her a reference to a 'second census,' and she begins pulling threads with genuine scholarly rigor. Beat: the antagonist becomes a mirror — another person serving a record she doesn't fully believe.

chapters.title: The Tower Full of Strangers
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Fugitives and witnesses named in the ledger begin arriving at the tower, sent by word of mouth: a deported man's widow, a mutinied sailor, a clerk who falsified manifests. Wendell takes their testimony, each voice a page verified. Beat: the found family swells into something like a congregation.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weighhouse
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. A trusted dockworker, terrified for his children, sells the group's meeting place to Cordelia's agents. A courier is seized with ledger pages; two witnesses flee the city. Beat: trust fractures; the group must decide whether mercy or security comes first.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Master
chapters.summary: Igeoma's POV. Cordelia confronts Igeoma directly, offering her a pardon and a restored guild position in exchange for the ledger. Igeoma refuses — and realizes Cordelia is not the true enemy but the instrument of one. She gives Wendell the guild's oldest secret: the master clock's chime mechanism can be rigged to carry sound across the whole city. Beat: the plan is born.

chapters.title: Forging the Record
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The group works in shifts to complete the verified ledger: testimony, documents, and a printed preamble Sefu sets by hand in a borrowed cellar press. Wendell realizes the ledger alone can be dismissed — it must be entered into the public record at the anniversary inquiry itself. Beat: quiet, exhausted resolve; the plan takes its final shape.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Doubt
chapters.summary: Cordelia's POV. Cross-referencing the seized pages, Cordelia confirms the scuttling order independently — and finds her own brother's name in the ledger's dead. Her commission's conclusions are lies, and she helped write them. Beat: the antagonist turns; she begins leaving gaps in the official history where the truth might be inserted.

chapters.title: The Sealing of the Archive
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The victors announce the official history will be sealed and archived on the anniversary, after which all riot records become state property — unreadable for fifty years. The deadline lands on the day the master clock will be rededicated, with Cordelia presiding. Beat: the trap of time snaps shut; one chance remains.

chapters.title: Rigging the Chime
chapters.summary: Wendell and Igeoma's POV. Wendell modifies the master clock: at the anniversary stroke, the chime will not merely ring but carry, through the tower's speaking-tubes, a human voice reading the ledger's preamble and names. The group rehearses in the dark, each taking pages. Beat: terror and tenderness — the clockmaker's craft turned into testimony.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Inquiry
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The rededication proceeds; the official history is read aloud to the assembled city. As the final seal is brought forward, Wendell steps from the clock mechanism housing, calls for right of testimony as a guild apprentice, and Cordelia — presiding — does not stop him. Beat: held breath; the whole book converges on a single room.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Names
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The chime strikes and the tower carries the voices: witness after witness, name after name, read into the inquiry's official transcript while the crowd and the soldiers listen. Cordelia enters the scuttling order into evidence herself, resigning her commission. Beat: catharsis — the dead are counted at last.

chapters.title: What the Victors Write
chapters.summary: Cordelia's POV. The inquiry cannot undo the regime, but the transcript is now part of the sealed archive — and Cordelia, dismissed but unrepentant, ensures copies reach foreign presses. She and Wendell meet once, two keepers of records, and part without friendship but with respect. Beat: victory that is partial, real, and costly.

chapters.title: The Clock Keeps Time
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A year later, Wendell is a journeyman clockmaker; Sefu's press reopens; the tower congregation has become a mutual-aid society. Wendell hides the original ledger inside the master clock again — not to bury it, but because the clock is the one place the city will always keep winding. He adds a new first page: his sister's name, in his own hand. Beat: belonging found, silence ended, the truth entrusted to time.
